description: Stereo multimode filter offering 35 filter modes and bypass, with zero-delay feedback topologies, 4x oversampled drive, and a jack for every control

params.text: Sets the gain into the filter, 0 to 100%, which is nothing at the bottom and 40dB at the top; the harder it is driven the more it soft-clips and the less the resonance peaks
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the DRIVE jack, -100% to +100%; at either end 10V covers the whole travel of the drive knob
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FREQ jack, -100% to +100%; at either end 10V covers the whole travel of the frequency knob
Sets the resonance, 0 to 100%, raising a peak in the response at the cutoff frequency
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the RES jack, -100% to +100%; at either end 10V covers the whole travel of the resonance knob
Blends the dry input with the filtered signal, 0 to 100% filtered, despite the manual describing this knob as a modulation rate

inputs.text: Adds to the drive knob, where 10V covers its whole travel once the drive attenuverter is open
Adds to the frequency knob, where 10V covers its whole travel once the frequency attenuverter is open, which puts the cutoff within a third of a semitone of a volt per octave
Adds to the resonance knob, where 10V covers its whole travel once the resonance attenuverter is open
Moves the filter mode on from the one chosen on the display, by three and a half modes per volt, and holds at the last of the 36 beyond that
Adds to the MIX knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
The left audio input into the filter
The right audio input into the filter

outputs.text: The left output, carrying dry and filtered signal in the proportion set by MIX
The right output, carrying dry and filtered signal in the proportion set by MIX

notes: clicking the mode display opens the 36 modes: bypass, two Sallen-Key, eight state variable, sixteen transistor ladder, a diode ladder, three dual resonator, two comb, FM, RM and a bitcrusher
each filter mode is named with its slope in dB per octave, and two modes of the same slope sound alike until the resonance is raised
a pole gives a slope of 6dB per octave, so a mode named 24 is a four-pole filter
the two comb modes feed a delayed copy of the signal back on itself, which is the mechanism behind chorus, phasing and flanging
the FM mode varies the frequency of the input with a sine wave
the RM mode varies the amplitude of the input with a sine wave
the bitcrusher mode reduces the sample rate and the bit depth of the input
the module is polyphonic and takes its channel count from whichever audio input carries more channels
